News.title: Man, 68, dies after hit-and-run on busy road in UK city as cops hunt motorist
News.content:
ROAD TRAGEDY Man, 68, dies after hit-and-run on busy road in UK city as cops hunt motorist

A MAN has been killed in a horror hit-and-run after being struck by a car near an Aldi supermarket.

The 68-year-old was walking when he was hit by a dark-coloured vehicle in Birmingham at around 8.45pm last night.

The driver then fled the scene, leaving the injured pedestrian behind.

The tragedy happened on Stratford Road in Hall Green, near Aldi and the junction with Wycome Road.





Despite desperate efforts by paramedics, the man was pronounced dead at the scene.

Cops have launched urgent enquiries to track down the car and identify the driver.

Detective Sergeant Julie Lyman, from the Serious Collision Investigation Unit, said: “Our thoughts today are with the family of the man who died, and we’re supporting his family.

“It’s vital that we identify the car and driver involved as soon as possible.



“If you are that driver, I’d urge you to do the right thing and come and call us straight away.

“If anyone who was in the area has mobile phone, dash cam or other footage from the time, we’d also like to speak to them as soon as possible.”

Police are appealing for anyone who witnessed the crash or captured footage to come forward.

Anyone with information can contact police via Live Chat on their website or by calling 101, quote log 5377 of September 3.

News.title: Hilarious moment newlywed couple lose their balance during a photoshoot and topple into river
News.content:
A BLUSHING bride and groom took a dip on their big day – plunging into a river in full wedding attire while having their photos taken.

Jamie Wade and Michelle, both 46, were posing for photos along the River Bure in Norfolk when they stood in a canoe.



But the newlyweds “went down like the Titanic” after losing their balance and made a splash at their August nuptials.

Jamie and Michelle, who was wearing a £1,800 gown, revealed the accident was part of a string of mishaps on their big day – but it didn’t dampen their spirits.



Phlebotomist Michelle said: “I can just remember, as we were sinking, thinking I can’t go in – I’ve got a wedding dress on, I’ve had my hair done.

“I’d only had that dress on two hours. We went down like the Titanic.



“We like the River Bure but I never thought I’d end up in it.

“Not exactly the elegant newlywed photo we had imagined, but somehow it sums up our day perfectly – completely unexpected, slightly chaotic, soaking wet, absolutely hilarious, and filled with love.”

Michelle and Jamie, a builder, first met at school in 1993 and entered a relationship before splitting as they went their separate ways as adults.

It was a chance meeting in a Tesco car park in 2016 when they met again and became engaged in May 2021 – on a boat.



Jamie said: “I’d moved back to Norfolk and went to Tesco one day when I saw Michelle walking through the car park.

“I had that panic moment that comes from childhood dreams and I thought ‘if I don’t talk to her now, I never will again’.

“We got engaged in 2021 on a boat and we’ve been inseparable ever since.

We’ve never spent more than a day apart.”



Their journey to the altar wasn’t easy as Michelle had suffered several miscarriages and an ectopic pregnancy.

The couple, of Horstead in Norfolk, planned to marry in 2025 but postponed following the heart breaking loss of Jamie’s dad and Michelle’s mum.

But despite everything the couple battled the odds to marry at Norwich Castle Museum on August 29 – with more hiccups than just the unexpected swim.

Jamie said: “First, Michelle forgot her bouquet and had to turn back, passing me on the road after we’d carefully avoided seeing each other all the night before.

“Then, as I cried my way through an emotional ceremony at Norwich Castle Museum, torrential rain caused the confetti to stick to all our guests as they threw it over us.



“It doesn’t rain for months and then the day you want to get married, the heavens open.”

Following the 50-guest wedding at Norwich Castle Museum, the couple held their reception at the Grade-II listed pub The King’s Head in Coltishall, Norfolk.

It was on the nearby Coltishall Common that their newlywed shoot began. Michelle said: “All morning we thought the weather looked okay and then suddenly, rain, thunder, everything.

“Our photographer told us we weren’t going to get our sunset picture but we knew we had to get creative. I’d waited since I was 13 for this moment.”

It was then the couple tentatively got into the canoe – before overbalancing and spilling into the river.



To make matters worse, another wedding guest had rushed to see if they were okay and slipped – breaking their leg.

The pair went back to their 120-strong wedding reception to the shock of their guests.

Jamie said: “We took it entirely in our stride. Michelle looked absolutely stunning before and after the dunk. She just shook out her drenched hair, straightened her dress, and gave me a big hug.

“I was tipping water out of my boots all night – every time I emptied them, a little while later they were full again.

“To top it off, Michelle accidentally put her foot in the fireworks machine and burnt her toe. If she hadn’t been wet, she would have gone up.



“We’d worked so hard to get to our wedding day and the powers that be had one last test for us.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The couple are due to go to Corfu on their honeymoon this month but

Michelle added: “I think we should probably take a paramedic.”

News.title: School boss who hoped Ofsted inspectors would ‘go under a lorry’ on ice & sent racist messages to colleagues is banned
News.content:
STRUCK OFF School boss who hoped Ofsted inspectors would ‘go under a lorry’ on ice & sent racist messages to colleagues is banned

A SCHOOL boss who hoped Ofsted inspectors would “go under a f****** lorry” on black ice has been banned from teaching.

Lee Hessey also branded parents “scrotes, vermin and pond life” and called one a “stupid cow”, a teaching panel heard.

The former chief executive of The Forge Academy Trust also sent racist messages to colleagues.

In one vile message, Lee wrote: “Ofsted. I hope they all go under a f****** lorry in some black ice tomorrow morning just in time for Christmas. Complete set of sh**bags.”





A Teacher Regulation Agency panel said it was “wholly inappropriate” for Lee to express a hope that Ofsted inspectors would die.

It found his language was “abusive, offensive and far removed from the standards expected of a headteacher”.

Lee was also found to have described parents as “low life”, “vermin” and a “bonkio parent”.

The panel said the remarks were derogatory and inappropriate, and could potentially impugn a person’s mental health.



It warned that public confidence in Lee and the wider teaching profession would be damaged if parents knew how he had referred to them.

Lee, who became CEO of the trust in September 2016, was responsible for six primary schools in Nottinghamshire.

But messages between him and two colleagues, sent between September 2022 and April 2023, contained a string of offensive comments.

In one, Lee wrote: “Buckingham Palace will be a lim city soon.”



The panel found this was a derogatory reference to Muslims.

In another message, he wrote: “A coloured character. Surprise, surprise.”

The panel also found the phrase “Bongo Bongo land” was an offensive and racist expression directed towards black or African people.

Lee was further found to have made references to “Tourette shoulder twitching”, which the panel regarded as mocking a disability.

The trust received complaints about Lee’s behaviour in 2023, including an allegation about his treatment of a pupil while he was interim headteacher during the 2021 to 2022 academic year.



During the investigation, the messages were disclosed and allegations were made that Lee had used inappropriate and discriminatory language.

The panel found no evidence that his actions were not deliberate or that he had been acting under extreme duress.

It said Lee was the most senior person in the messaging group and should have been setting the standard.

The panel added that even if the group’s tone had encouraged inappropriate “banter”, this did not lessen Lee’s responsibility.

It said there was “substantial evidence” of his positive contributions to schools in deprived communities and that he had achieved “significant improvements”.



The panel did not initially suggest that Lee should be banned indefinitely.

But a senior TRA official acting on behalf of the Education Secretary overruled that decision.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A prohibition order was deemed “proportionate” and in the “public interest”.

Lee is now banned indefinitely from teaching in any school, sixth form college, relevant youth accommodation or children’s home in England.

News.title: Moment convicted murderer kidnaps girl, 15, at knifepoint before sexually assaulting her in eight-hour horror ordeal
News.content:
THIS is the horrifying moment a convicted murderer kidnaps a 15-year-old girl at knifepoint before sexually assaulting her in an eight-hour ordeal.

Paul Sharpe, 56, bundled the teen into a car as she walked through Altrincham in Greater Manchester, on May 18 at around 7.30pm.



Police have since released CCTV footage showing the moment the vile killer grabs the girl and forces her into his motor.

Footage shows the silver car driving along a residential road, as the girl walks past.



The car passes the gates of a house before disappearing behind some hedges.

A man in high-vis can then be seen walking up to the gates of the property before crossing back over towards the girl.



The girl and the man then disappear from sight behind a hedgerow and later footage shows the silver motor driving off.

Video shows the vehicle travelling along several roads before eventually coming into a car park.



Police bodycam footage then shows the moment officers pull up alongside the silver car and find Sharpe in the back seat.

He is pulled from the motor and arrested by responding officers before he’s bundled into the back of a police van.

Sharpe was previously jailed for strangling his wife to death in 2000 after she threatened to break up with him.

During the harrowing ordeal he tied up the girl’s wrists and feet and abused her after grabbing her off the street.

Minshull Street Crown Court heard the local radio DJ drove to an airport car park after kidnapping the girl.



He then moved around different car parks in the area and forced the teen to drink alcohol before sexually assaulting her in a harrowing eight-hour ordeal.

He has now been jailed for life with a minimum of eight years after he pleaded guilty to six offences including kidnapping, sexual assault and threats with a blade.

Police launched a probe after the teen was reported missing and investigators trawled through CCTV.



Cops eventually tracked Sharpe to a hotel car park in Knutsford, Cheshire – around seven miles from where the girl was last seen.

In a police interview, the killer claimed he was “feeling bad” and believed it would be easier to kidnap a child rather than an adult.

Sharpe also told officers he intended to release her when it got light and then take his own life.

He claimed his motives weren’t sexual, but admitted to being aroused after smelling his victim’s feet.

A CPS spokesperson previously said: “In this terrifying incident the victim was held captive for eight hours while Sharpe forced her to drink alcohol and sexually assaulted her.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Sharpe gave no thought to the impact his actions, for his own depraved reasons, would have on his victim.

“Although his guilty pleas today have spared her from the ordeal of a trial, I would like to thank the girl and her family for supporting this prosecution and ensuring this dangerous offender is back where he belongs.”

News.title: Labour MP whose husband faces ‘China spy’ probe enjoys secret trysts with married Holyrood figure
News.content:
A LABOUR MP whose husband is accused of spying for China has been enjoying trysts with a married Holyrood figure, we can reveal.

Joani Reid, 40, was spotted sharing cosy meals and staying overnight with the high-profile man in her East Kilbride constituency.



It comes as lobbyist spouse David Taylor, 39, remains at the centre of a Met Police counter- terrorism probe on suspicion of “targeting UK democracy”.

Reid revealed she had returned to the party’s ranks amid a China spying scandal hours after her overnight stay with the high-profile Holyrood figure.



The Scot announced she’d had the whip restored at Westminster four months after husband David Taylor was arrested on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service.

But we can reveal Reid, 40, had a series of public meet-ups in her East Kilbride constituency with a married man who is well known in the Scottish Parliament.

The revelations also come after she was accused of being “flirty” with two naval officers at Faslane nuclear subs base on the Clyde.

Details of her affair with the parliament-linked man sparked a claim Reid’s “reckless” behaviour could leave her open to “compromise and blackmail”.



She had voluntarily suspended herself from Labour’s Commons group on March 5 but revealed her return in an online statement on the evening of Thursday, July 30.

But just hours earlier Reid and the married man had been seen leaving her flat — the morning after they had dined out together.

The pair had been spotted at 7.30pm on the Wednesday at Zucca restaurant in East Kilbride, close to Reid’s office and home.

At 8.55pm, they were pictured together walking the short distance to her pad. Reid was wearing a pink North Face jacket and blue jeans.

The man had on a pair of jeans plus a beige jacket with hood.



He was spotted leaving the MP’s property at 8.45am the following morning in the same outfit.

Around 30 minutes later, Reid left in her motor and made the short drive to her constituency office. She wore a blue skirt with flat animal print shoes and a denim jacket.

And Reid appeared to have the same outfit on ten hours later as she announced her comeback in a video posted on social media.



She told her 1,202 followers on Instagram: “I just wanted everyone to know my suspension from the Labour Party has now been lifted and I’m back as a Labour MP.

“It brings to an end a really difficult period for me and I wanted to say thank you to all the people and constituents who got in touch with messages of support and kindness.

“And finally I just wanted to remind and reassure you that I have never been part of a police investigation, either as a suspect or even as a witness.”

The Scottish Sun also has evidence that the man — who we are not naming for legal reasons — met with Reid twice last month.

They were spotted inside East Kilbride’s Mata Hari restaurant, after Reid joined fellow Labour members at a bash to back MSP Joe Fagan’s bid to be elected as the party’s next Scottish leader.



Rocked by six months of turmoil BY CHRIS TAYLOR THE latest controversy involving Joani Reid comes just over two years after she became a Labour MP at the July 2024 General Election. She’d told earlier how she had been inspired to stand for the East Kilbride and Strathaven seat while watching TV with her gran — who said she was “very concerned” for the country’s future. And during the campaign, she told voters she knew “the challenges that local families face” and insisted that the “community deserves better”. After husband David Taylor was arrested in March over claims of spying for China, Reid said she was not part of his “business activities”. But accounts for her now-liquidated firm Reid Strategy revealed she received nearly £24,000 in interest-free loans from two companies where he was listed as a director. In 2022 her consultancy business had assets of just £2,870. A year later they were £442,103, with shareholders’ funds rocketing from £1,351 to £311,836. The firm was dissolved in August last year.

The pair later spent some time in her flat before the man left a short time later, wearing a baseball cap. He then made his way to his motor in a public car park. On one occasion he was also seen walking to the door of Reid’s flat while she took a phone call in the garden.

The apartment is a short distance from the four-bedroom family home in the town’s St Leonards that was searched as part of the ongoing investigation into her husband by the Met’s counter-terrorism cops.

A source said Reid was now “estranged” from Taylor, but the Holyrood figure she was involved with still lives with his wife.

Last night Scottish Tory leader Russell Findlay said: “Following her husband’s arrest over allegations that he spied for China, this Labour MP’s own conduct has already been under the spotlight. So for her to engage in such risky and reckless behaviour further calls into question her judgment and that of her party.



“Hostile states like Russia and China are seeking to undermine our country, which means all elected representatives have a responsibility to be alert to the risk of compromise and blackmail.”

We told in March how Taylor, 39, was one of three men arrested on suspicion of spying for China and “targeting UK democracy”.

The lobbyist was held in London while PR firm boss Matthew Aplin, 43, an a 68-year-old unnamed man were nabbed in Wales.

Reid — who is a granddaughter of the late shipyard union boss Jimmy Reid — has said repeatedly she never saw anything to make her suspect her husband had broken the law.

High-flyer influence REID is one of 11 MPs sitting on Westminster’s Home Affairs Select Committee, which has launched inquiries into organised crime, security and combating extremism. She joined the panel just months after being elected and continued as a member during her Labour suspension. The granddaughter of late Clydeside union legend Jimmy Reid graduated in politics and philosophy from Glasgow Uni before leaving the city to obtain a masters degree in public policy in London. Reid was a councillor in Lewisham from 2014-2022 but returned to Scotland to stand in East Kilbride and Strathaven. She got 22,682 votes in the 2024 election, securing a 9,057 majority over the SNP candidate Grant Costello.



The Metropolitan Police said in May that all three suspects would remain on bail.

Reid insisted in March: “I have never been to China. I have never spoken on China or China-related matters in the Commons.

“I have never asked a question on China-related matters.”

Her Welsh husband is director of policy at Asia House, a think-tank which say is dedicated to “fostering meaningful dialogue between Asia, the Middle East, and Europe”.

He was previously a special adviser to Labour Welsh Secretary Peter Hain from 2009 to 2010.



Last November Taylor was pictured shaking hands with former Chinese minister Jin Liqun, who was then boss of Beijing-based Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank.

Reid, an MP since July 2024, went on: “I have never seen anything to make me suspect my husband has broken any law. I am not part of my husband’s business activities.”

It emerged this April that she had been accused of inappropriate behaviour with two senior Royal Navy officers. Reid allegedly was “all over” one of the men during a drunken night in the officers’ mess at the Faslane base in Argyll.

She left the Armed Forces Parliamentary Scheme following the alleged incident last year.

An MP said they reported Reid due to fears that information about Britain’s nuclear deterrent could end up in enemy hands.



But a senior source said they were satisfied there was “no link” to the China spy case.

Separately, it was reported that a married submarine captain stepped down following another probe into a suspected relationship with Reid.

Insiders said allegations of “flirtatious” messages were probed by Navy chiefs and the captain was not found to have broken any rules.

In April, Nats MP Kirsty Blackman said the China spying claims and later revelations were “a scandal of unprecedented proportions”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

At the time, a source close to Reid said allegations of national security concerns due to her behaviour were “opportunistic hypocrisy — as shown by the nearly a year gap between the events and the report”.



We approached Reid but she declined to comment, as did Labour. The man did not respond to requests for comment.

News.title: Javier Milei proposes using Hong Kong-style handover as model for bringing Falkland Islands under Argentine control
News.content:
ARGENTINA’S president has called for the UK to give them a Hong Kong-style handover of the Falkland Islands.

Javier Milei’s brazen demands come amid speculation the US may support Buenos Aires over their nonsensical claims to the British territory.



The Argentine tyrant called for a “consensus solution” and claimed his people “do not believe in war”.

But the nationalist firebrand announced on Thursday plans for a new military base and slammed Britain as a country “in decline”.



He told The Economist: “The UK did this with Hong Kong, so why not find the agreement so that sooner or later the islands return to Argentina? They’re ours.”

Milei appeared to be referencing the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration – an agreement between the UK and China to gradually put the city back under Beijing‘s control from 1997 onwards.



The former British colony was reintegrated into China’s national territory but has been allowed to keep its own political system for 50 years.

Hong Kongers were never allowed a vote on the deal.



China has also been accused of violating the Joint Declaration due to its authoritarian crackdown on political dissent.

It comes after Donald Trump suggested he would not back the UK if Argentina invaded the archipelago, citing the lack of support in the war on Iran.

The fears follow a leak of an internal Pentagon email in April implying the US may review its position on the islands.



Milei has recently insisted the islands are a crucial part of Argentina’s “future”, while announcing sanctions on oil companies working off the islands “under the British occupation”.

He warned the UK is facing “multiple crises” that are “unlikely to be resolved” while “Argentina‘s future is flourishing and will prevail”.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband denounced Milei’s outlandish claim, as he doubled down on Britain’s “unwavering position”.

And the Falkland Islanders themselves have put two fingers up to Milei by insisting they want to stay British.

They dismissed “threats and claims” as old hat on Friday and vowed to press on development – code for drilling for oil off the coast.



In a statement the islands Legislative Assembly said their right to be British was enshrined in law and would not be threatened by leaders’ hot air.

They said: “Our future is a matter for the people who live here to decide. That is a right grounded in international law, and it is not altered by the statements of any other government.”

A 2013 referendum saw 99.8 per cent of islanders voted to remain a self-governing Overseas Territory of the United Kingdom.

In Argentina, many have accused Milei of using the Falklands to distract the public from his political woes – including the struggling economy and accusations of corruption.

He has helped tame inflation and reduce welfare spending – but the path has left many jobless and without benefits.
