Sports.title: Furious soccer fans unveil Times Square billboard calling for Gianni Infantino to be ousted as they accuse embattled FIFA President of blackmail
Sports.content:
Angry soccer fans have taken to Times Square, unveiling a massive billboard calling for FIFA President Gianni Infantino to be removed after recent controversies.

Infantino sparked outrage long before the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States after giving President Donald Trump a newly created 'FIFA Peace Prize', before inviting Trump to present the trophy to the winning team.

Since then, his clandestine plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to Joshua Kushner has been uncovered and faced huge backlash from fans around the world.

In the wake of The Times revealing the devious scheme, that would have banked him millions, Infantino has faced calls to resign and threats of boycotts from governing bodies, led by UEFA.

And soccer fans from around the world have now unveiled a Times Square billboard in New York City demanding he resign. The billboard went live at 6am ET on September 4, on the corner of 1500 Broadway and West 43rd Street.

Organizers said: 'We are football fans first and foremost and believe we echo the feelings of fans everywhere regarding Infantino and the threat he poses to the future of football.

Gianna Infantino is facing ongoing pressure in his role as FIFA President after recent revelations

Soccer fans have funded a Times Square billboard demanding Infantino be ousted from his role

Organizers of the billboard have accused the embattled President of 'blackmail'

'He deceived, blackmailed, and threatened FIFA, his team and the wider global football leadership in order to sell international football to people who have ties to deeply unsavory activities, and who have no interest in the fans except as profit centers.

'It is transparent to us that Kushner and his associates want to own the 'assets' of football – the fans and the players – to use as they wish while simultaneously wielding the soft power of international football as a tool of control.

'Infantino, who is meant to protect football from such grave dangers, enthusiastically offered it up on a platter, paving the way with a fake 'Peace Prize', and only stipulating that he gets a cut. Shameful.

'We call on fans everywhere to make it clear Infantino is persona non grata at their stadiums and to demand the confederations they're members of remove him as soon as possible.

'Until he is removed, we demand action: We call on federations and confederations to revoke invitations and/or ban Infantino from tournaments and matches

'We call on the football community to let Infantino know he's not welcome by demonstrating against him at matches and any football related events, by unveiling tifos calling for his removal and by boycotting FIFA events.

'Gianni Infantino is not a leader, he is a dealer who tried to sell the World Cup and more disturbingly, the children's World Cup. We should all be shocked and disgusted by the latter.'

FIFA recently accused UEFA of a 'smear campaign' after legal applications made to access documents related to FIFA's controversial private investor plan. UEFA is applying through the American courts for discovery of evidence and documentation linked to FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), a private company which it was envisaged would run the World Cup and other FIFA competitions.

The billboard appeared on Friday morning in Times Square demanding 'Infantino Out'

Infantino and Trump made another public appearance at the FIFA World Cup Final in July

Infantino was recently tracked down in the Caribbean and confronted over calls to resign and claims he has 'betrayed the game'.

Not giving an answer to Sky News reporter James Matthews, he simply joked: 'You have a nice haircut.'

He repeatedly said 'thank you very much' as he neared the car. Then, as security personnel prepared to close the door, Infantino turned back towards Matthews and finished with another hair-related joke: 'I'll see you at the hairdressers.'

Sports.title: Charlie Woods adds to stunning NIL wealth as he inks new deal with one of the world's biggest golf brands
Sports.content:
Charlie Woods adds to stunning NIL wealth as he inks new deal with one of the world's biggest golf brands

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Charlie Woods has signed a deal with TaylorMade, one of golf's biggest brands, in the latest boost to his huge NIL fortune.

Woods was unveiled as the brand's newest signing in a social media video showing him putting on his golf spikes in the locker room then putting on a TaylorMade hat.

'Just getting started. Welcome to the squad, Charlie Woods,' the brand wrote. The news was announced while Woods was putting in a strong performance at the American Junior Golf Association Junior Players, shooting a one-under first round to sit tied-seventh on the leaderboard.

The nature of the deal with TaylorMade is unclear. His dad, 15-time major champion Tiger Woods, still has a deal with the brand and uses their clubs. Top PGA Tour stars including Rory McIlroy, Scottie Scheffler, Tommy Fleetwood and Collin Morikawa are with TaylorMade.

However, Tiger Woods now has his own clothing brand - Sun Day Red - which has been worn by Charlie in the past. It is unclear if his TaylorMade deal will include clothing as well as equipment.

Either way, it is the latest big deal the son of 15-time major champion Tiger Woods has secured before even turning professional.

Tiger Woods' son Charlie has landed another huge deal, this time with TaylorMade Golf

Woods already has a host of NIL deals ahead of starting college at Florida State University

According to The Caddie Network, Woods already had an estimated NIL valuation of $3 million, per their latest Collegiate Golf NIL market values.

Woods recently started his final high school golf season and is committed to Florida State University.

The 17-year-old has won two high school state championships with his team, and his first ever AJGA junior title actually came in the AJGA Team TaylorMade Invitational in 2025.

He already has the highest golf NIL valuation since rankings were introduced in 2024, with his star power and big social media following giving him commercial appeal only rivaled by Kai Trump.

The granddaughter of the President, who boasts three million followers on Instagram, ranked second on the list with an estimated NIL valuation of $2.25 million.

Kai is the daughter of Vanessa Trump, who is dating Charlie's father, meaning the combined families dominate the rankings.

Charlie is reportedly represented by Players Group Management for NIL opportunities, and has long been tipped to cash-in on his family status.

His high school coach, Toby Harbeck, told the Palm Beach Post in 2024: 'I'm sure someone's going to approach him with NIL.

'They're so smart and they've got such good people around them that I think the only thing we need to be careful of is making sure we're all aware of what's going on.'

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola 'never doubted' Cody Gakpo despite nearly completing Liverpool exit
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola 'never doubted' Cody Gakpo despite nearly completing Liverpool exit

Cody Gakpo played a starring role, creating both of Alexander Isak's goals, as Liverpool recorded their first Premier League win of the Andoni Iraola era

View 2 Images Cody Gakpo celebrates with Alexander Isak during Liverpool's win over Ipswich

Andoni Iraola insists he never doubted Cody Gakpo even after the Liverpool forward nearly quit Anfield.

‌



Gakpo could have left in the final days of the transfer window after Manchester City launched a bid to sign him but Liverpool blocked the move after failing to find replacements.

‌



Holland international Gakpo provided both assists for two-goal Alexander Isak in what was Liverpool’s first win under Iraola.

‌



Liverpool boss Iraola said: “Cody knows how much we value him. There is no doubt. I rate him very highly. There might be, obviously, strong competition for minutes because we have good players there in those positions.

“It's a matter of pushing each other. With Bradley Barcola, with Rio Ngumoha, with Victor Munoz, it's a matter of sometimes they will start, sometimes they will come from the bench, sometimes they will not play, but this is competition.

‌

“Cody has been very good all preseason. He started the season very well, producing numbers today. Then after the two assists, he finishes as number nine to help us close the game.

“I think it's good to have Cody because he can play in three positions up top, like other of our players. To have him in this place for this particular position is good.”

‌



Iraola was also full of praise for Isak who has now got three goals this season which is as many as he got for Liverpool in the entire Premier League campaign last year. Bradley Barcola also got his debut as a substitute after his £106m move.

It also marked Iraola’s first win as Liverpool manager and he admitted he was relieved to get it after two draws in their opening fixtures.

Iraola added: “If he's fit, if he's available, if he's in a good shape, I think he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. Probably, it will be about other things.

‌



View 2 Images Gakpo played a starring role in the win over Ipswich

“I will demand other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. The goals will come. I think he has to contribute to the collective. And when everyone helps, I think the goals and the result will come.

“Bradley has not played a single minute since the World Cup, so we needed to be careful. I’m happy because 30 minutes is going to be good for his fitness for his build-up, and we will continue because now we play a lot of games. So he will have the chance to play.

‌



"I think two points also don't reflect our two first games. So definitely, we couldn't lose anymore and I’m happy because I think we controlled it well today.”

Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil insisted he was happy with his team and “proud of his players.” He added: “After the first two goals, we recovered and matched them and were arguably the better team at times.”

Sports.title: Virgil van Dijk makes feelings very clear on Cody Gakpo after Liverpool exit U-turn
Sports.content:
Virgil van Dijk makes feelings very clear on Cody Gakpo after Liverpool exit U-turn

Cody Gakpo has been key to Liverpool so far under Andoni Iraola but the Dutchman might not have been at Anfield after all had a move to Manchester City been completed over the final days of the window

View 2 Images

Virgil van Dijk insists Cody Gakpo will continue to be crucial to Liverpool after his failed move to Manchester City. The Dutchman was thought to be on the way out of Anfield over the final days of the transfer window.

‌



Tottenham Hotspur had been credited as admirers, only to be gazumped by Premier League rivals Manchester City. Gakpo even went as far as approving a switch to the Etihad Stadium.

‌



But for various reasons - including Liverpool’s inability to find a replacement - his switch was not completed. The Reds might be thankful of that fact given how key the Dutch forward has been to Liverpool.

‌



He netted on the opening day of the season and followed that up with an assist against Nottingham Forest. Gakpo then set up Alexander Isak twice against Ipswich on Friday evening.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Speaking after that game, club and international teammate Virgil van Dijk was full of praise. Asked how important Gakpo has been, he said: “Massively.

‌



“Obviously I said before the transfer window was closed that he’s important for us and he will be important for us this season as well. And he showed it again today. Last week as well with the assists, over the last couple of years as well. So keep going.”

Sports.title: Liverpool transfer call vindicated as Alexander Isak downs Ipswich - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Liverpool finally secured their first win of the Premier League season by beating newly-promoted Ipswich at Portman Road.

Liverpool took control early on through Alexander Isak as he scored twice in the opening ten minutes. The Reds thought they were set to be handed a penalty after Dominik Szoboszlai was fouled midway through the second-half but VAR correctly intervened.

But the damage was already done in the first half by Isak, as Liverpool sealed their first success of the campaign, while it's now back-to-back defeats for Ipswich.

Here are all of the talking points from Portman Road:

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Isak back to his best

Barely six minutes into the game and Liverpool were ahead through Isak. A lot of the praise for the goal has to go to Cody Gakpo, who showed great feet in the centre of the park and picked out the Swedish forward with an inch-perfect ball.

He controlled and then hammered past Kjell Scherpen in the Ipswich goal, who may have thought he could have done better. But Isak will not care too much, having netted his second goal of the season.

Two became three barely three minutes later as he latched onto another brilliant pass by Gakpo, composed himself and slotted home. He's now matched his Premier League goal record from the entirety of last season and it would be foolish to bet against him beating that.

‌



He actually thought he had done after getting on the end of a Florian Wirtz cross but had drifted offside.

View 3 Images Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo linked up well at Ipswich (Image: Getty Images)

Gakpo call spot on

If things had panned out differently, Liverpool might not have had Cody Gakpo's services to call upon for this game. He appeared set for a move to Manchester City over the closing days of the window.

For one reason or another, the move did not come to fruition. Liverpool will be hugely thankful that it didn't. Gakpo's passes for Isak were brilliant - the first being an inch-perfect pass, the second being a brilliant, outside of the boot effort.

‌



Like Isak, Gakpo has really impressed over the opening weeks of the campaign and that was certainly the same at Portman Road.

Penalty decision explained

Liverpool thought they were going to be given a golden opportunity to extend their lead even further as Dominik Szoboszlai was taken down by Leif Davies.

The referee did not give the decision initially but looked as though he would change his mind upon review. But the hosts still had a reprieve, with the Liverpool midfielder offside in the build-up, rendering the controversy irrelevant in any case.

It might not have been the call that Liverpool wanted, but it was the correct one.

‌



View 3 Images Dominik Szoboszlai thought he had won a penalty against Ipswich (Image: Getty Images)

Barcola gets Premier League introduction

While Liverpool fans will have been keen to see their side win, another key moment that they were looking forward to was Bradley Barcola's debut. The Frenchman was named on the bench following his £123m move from PSG.

But he came on in the second period to make his bow. In honesty, he was on the periphery of the game but there were a few moments where he showed his electric pace in front of the away fans so they will certainly be keen to see that a lot more throughout his time on Merseyside.

First win, first clean sheet

Liverpool's defensive frailties have been well discussed this season. And they were on show once again at Portman Road. The hosts managed to get through on a few occasions, with it taking either an important intervention from Jeremy Jacquet or a save from Alisson to keep them out.

‌



Regardless, Liverpool finally have their first win and first clean sheet of the campaign and that will be a big relief to Andoni Iraola.

When it comes to Ipswich, their season will of course not be defined against games against Liverpool - or indeed last week's trip to Old Trafford - so they won't be too worried at all.

Sports.title: Jockey ‘steals race’ after horse whips round and false start flag raised
Sports.content:
Jockey ‘steals race’ after horse whips round and false start flag raised

A stewards inquiry was called to investigate the confusion at the start of a race in which Dark Tide Rising is afforded a huge advantage to win the bumper race by 15 lengths

View 4 Images Confusion at Worcester: Kielan Woods (front) looks back at the start as the flag man waves his flag ahead (Image: @AtTheRaces)

A jockey was able to steal a huge lead and win a race unchallenged after taking advantage of a chaotic start to a race at Worcester on Friday.

‌



Punters questioned whether the 2m National Hunt Flat Race should have been declared void after Dark Tide Rising coasted to a 15 lengths victory under Kielan Woods.

‌



The confusion began when Company Charge, who was making his debut for Nigel and Willy Twiston-Davies, whipped round to the left and unshipped jockey Sam Twiston-Davies, Dark Tide Rising went off into a clear lead while the rest of the field appeared to hesitate after the flag man waved his flag up ahead, the usual signal of a false start.

‌



Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe to be open to geldings from 2027 after major rule change READ MORE :

Woods and other riders glanced behind them at the starter in the confusion but when the flag was lowered, they started to race, by which time Dark Tide Rising was left with a clear and ultimately unassailable advantage.

Watching a replay of the start Sky Sports Racing reporter Luke Harvey said: “The flag man’s confused so he waves his flag. Kielan Woods looks around. He’s looked around at the starter who hasn’t waved his flag, which means the race is going ahead and Kielan Woods has quite literally stolen this.

"There was a fair amount of controversy there but you can't take away a brilliant ride by Kielan Woods."

‌



View 4 Images The stewards ruled that the result of the race stood (Image: @AtTheRaces)

Woods said: “The flag went down. Sammy’s horse obviously unseated him. I seen the flag man hold his flag up and then he’s dropped it down."

The stewards called an inquiry into the start of the race which also considered "why the Advanced Flag Operator (AFO) appeared to briefly wave the recall flag before lowering it and walking away, despite there very clearly being no instruction from the Starter that a false start had been called."

‌



Twiston-Davies, Sean Bowen, Woods, Lewis Stones, Freddie Keighley, Lee Edwards, Tristan Durrell, James Best and Harry Cobden were interviewed as well as the two BHA starters and the AFO.

View 4 Images Dark Tide Rising coasted to a 15 length victory (Image: @AtTheRaces)

The report said: "Having heard their evidence, the Stewards were satisfied that a fair start had been affected, before COMPANY CHANGE veered violently left-handed after the starting tape released, resulting in Twiston-Davies being unseated.

‌



"After this had occurred Woods had sent DARK TIDE RISING (IRE) forward to make the running but at the same time EBARAYNA, which was initially sitting in the slipstream of DARK TIDE RISING (IRE) had baulked when reacting to the unseated horse and in jamming on had effectively interfered with the rest of the field to varying degrees, which greatly assisted DARK TIDE RISING (IRE) in establishing a sizeable advantage through the early stages.

View 4 Images Kielan Woods: rode the winner of the race at Worcester

"All riders with the exception of Lee Edwards explained that they were in little doubt as to whether or not they should continue in the race despite seeing the AFO briefly wave his flag, as they had a clear view of the senior starter for several seconds and he never gave indication that he was raising his flag, nor was the whistle blown by the AFO, which under the rules must accompany any recall flag being waved.

Article continues below

"Edwards explained that after his mount had surrendered several lengths of its own accord due to being spooked by the riderless horse, he chased EBARAYNA along to get it into stride before briefly being unsure whether a false start had been called after seeing the AFO waving his flag.

"He added that in the overall context of this race and given his beaten margin, it was unlikely that any period of indecision had materially affected his chances. Therefore, the Stewards confirmed the result and ordered a report to be forwarded to the Head Office of the British Horseracing Authority."

Sports.title: Aryna Sabalenka forced to halt US Open clash after complaining that 'someone is smoking weed'
Sports.content:
Aryna Sabalenka forced to halt US Open clash after complaining that 'someone is smoking weed'

Aryna Sabalenka took on Kamilla Rakhimova in the third round of the US Open on Friday, when the WTA No. 1 was forced to halt proceedings due to the smell of cannabis in the air

View Image Aryna Sabalenka was put off by the smell of weed during her US Open match (Image: Getty Images)

Aryna Sabalenka was forced to briefly pause her US Open match with Kamilla Rakhimova due to a strong smell of cannabis. The WTA No. 1 was 3-0 up in the first set against her Uzbek opponent on Friday, when she complained: "Someone is smoking weed," to umpire, Eva Asderaki-Moore.

‌



The referee was asked to intervene as a result of the "strong" odour, with Asderaki-Moore quickly contacting an official on her radio. She was also spotted making a smoking gesture to someone behind her.

‌



Play quickly continued, as Sabalenka ran out to a 6-3 6-4 win in New York, storming into Sunday's fourth round. However, Sabalenka is not the only athlete to have complained about the smell at Flushing Meadows.

‌



US Open make huge Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz announcement READ MORE :

Boulter explained: "Yeah, I have experienced it. You go down to the practice courts and down in the park courts, you do smell it a lot.

"I mean it’s not great. We’ll find out how the practice goes. If it goes well or not, I don’t know. We’ll see.

"But I’m not a huge fan of it. I know a lot of players have complained on some of the specific courts.

Sports.title: Incredible story of striker who went backpacking and ended up in the Premier League
Sports.content:
Brighton striker Promise David admitted he thought it was a “scam” when he was offered his first big break.

The Canada World Cup star had been backpacking around Europe when the call came two years ago which would change his career and take him from the Estonian Third Division into the Premier League.

Belgian club Union Saint-Gilloise - where Brighton owner Tony Bloom is a shareholder - identified David from their scouting system and the rest is history.

David was at Estonian club Nomme Kalju at the time - often playing for their under-21s - when the call came and he has ended up going to Brighton in a potential £22m deal via Belgium.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

David, 25, said: “They’ve got a great data scout system, that’s all I can say. They picked me out of thin air, but they said they had been monitoring me for a while.

“At first, I thought it was spam, like a scam. Because if you’re playing in the third division in Estonia, you don’t expect a team playing in the Europa League to call. But they did and I went. A couple of months in, I was having the best times of my life.

‌



“Me and my agent at the time both saw it and I was like, ‘Nah, it’s not that.’ And then we sat on a Zoom call and I said, ‘Oh s***, it is them’.

“They gave me a whole pitch, but I said yes before the pitch. It’s like sitting in a job interview and you’ve already accepted the job, telling all this bulls***, and I’m already there.

View 3 Images From the Estonian third division to facing Chelsea at Stamford Bridge

“I was packing my suitcases mid-call, trying to think how I was going to box everything together. And then, two weeks later, I was in Belgium.”

‌



His story is amazing. And he admits that maybe his laid back attitude - enjoying life and taking in Europe as he went from club to club - helped because he did not feel so much pressure. Born in Ontario, a stint in USA, played in Croatia, Malta an Estonia before Belgium and now England.

“I was just backpacking and having fun playing football through Europe. And seeing where things would take me next. I couldn’t fit in or stay long anywhere and I just kept packing my bags and moving on,” he said.

“I was just enjoying playing football through Europe. Not really thinking what would come of it. Just thinking about my next meal. It got a little bit serious in Estonia.

"I found a really good place. Actually, I didn’t find a good place. A good place found me at Union Saint-Gilloise. There, I was able to train like a professional and live like a professional. And good things came out of it. And then, boom, here I am.”

‌



View 3 Images Promise David in World Cup action for Canada (Image: Getty Images)

He is such a likeable person. Smiling and good fun. He is also clearly very talented. He showed up on the scouting apps after scoring 30 goals in 44 first team games in Estonia.

Forty one goals in 82 games for USG followed and now he is at Brighton where is on a season-long loan with an obligation to buy if he hits expectation levels.

But he also feels no added pressure. “Same s***, different day,” he said. “It’s the same thing, different stadium. Same game I was playing four years ago, just different stadium, different opponents.

‌



“I’m just hoping to bring goals. I think I’m a very unique player. As long as I can just catch up, I think I’ll be fine. I’m pretty good in the box, in terms of finding balls and just being in the right spaces at the right time.

“Very good hold-up play. I like to play with my back to goal against big centre-backs and being able to advance the team forward. I’m pretty tall, so in the air I like to get up there.”

Mind you, David has already proved he is ready for the big stage in front of huge attendances and go further than ever before. He played - and scored - for Canada in the World Cup and enjoyed the experience which was all the more special as he came pretty close to missing the tournament.

‌



He added: “I got injured in February, I was out for three months. And then your first game back is World Cup game one in your home country. But it was a great experience.

“I think every game we broke records. With the national team, all of us know each other from young. You want to see old friends and being able to train together, so it’s pretty good.”

Sports.title: Nicky Henderson admits Constitution Hill has a 'very hard task in front of him'
Sports.content:
Nicky Henderson admits Constitution Hill has a 'very hard task in front of him'

Constitution Hill will bid to continue his Flat career in the William Hill September Stakes at Kempton Park on Saturday, but Nicky Henderson's nine-year-old faces a significant challenge against Group 1-rated rivals

View 2 Images (Image: Alan Crowhurst, Getty Images)

Constitution Hill has a 'very hard task in front of him', his trainer Nicky Henderson has admitted.

‌



Kempton Park has played a pivotal role in the story of the one-time superstar jumper, and Saturday will be no different, as he faces his sternest test yet in his new career as a Flat horse in the William Hill September Stakes.

‌



The nine-year-old lit up Boxing Day at the Sunbury venue for three successive years, claiming a hat-trick of victories in the Christmas Hurdle between 2022 and 2024. But the winner of the 2023 Champion Hurdle switched codes in February after a sequence of three falls in four races.

‌



Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe to be open to geldings from 2027 after major rule change READ MORE :

Top trainers Alan King and Lucinda Russell 'named' by government for underpaying workers READ MORE :

He recorded a stunning win at Southwell, scoring by seven lengths before a record crowd for the Nottinghamshire track. Then he won another novice stakes at Kempton in March and is ready to resume his new career following a short break.

Saturday's seven-runner field is headed by Arc-bound Gethin and Group 1 winner Tornado Alert, who are officially rated more than a stone superior. Billy Loughnane takes the ride for the first time.

‌



"The important thing is to get a run into him because that will determine where we're going to go," Henderson told talkSPORT2. "He's got a handicap mark, but you have to have a third run to get into those handicaps that he could go for – when you're rated over 100, you can't get in with two runs.

View 2 Images Constitution Hill is back in action under Billy Loughnane at Kempton (Image: PA)

"He's had five months since his last run. So this race will bring him on quite a lot. It's not going to be the biggest excuse in the world that he's not ready. He's ready. But he's taking on young horses.

Article continues below

"We're nine years old and he's taking on Group 1 Flat horses. On ratings, we've got to improve over a stone.

"He's come back looking fantastic. He's done plenty of work. I'd like to have had a spin on the grass at some stage, but as every trainer in the country would tell you, you can't do that at the moment.

"So we've got to go here and it's on the all-weather. So we know the ground is OK, but he's got a very hard task in front of him. But we're up and ready for it. I say this will tell us where we belong, where he goes from here."

Sports.title: Julian Alvarez transfer saga in fresh twist as Man City 'made £129m bid' to hijack Arsenal
Sports.content:
Julian Alvarez transfer saga in fresh twist as Man City 'made £129m bid' to hijack Arsenal

Details have emerged of a supposed late effort by Manchester City to scupper Arsenal's hunt for Julian Alvarez ahead of deadline day

View 2 Images Manchester City reportedly tried to sign Julian Alvarez late in the transfer window (Image: Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Manchester City tried to hijack Arsenal’s pursuit of Julian Alvarez with a £128million offer last week, according to reports in Spain. One of the biggest and most drawn-out transfer sagas reached its anti-climactic conclusion on Tuesday as Alvarez opted to stay at Atletico Madrid.

‌



Over the course of the summer, the 26-year-old striker had repeatedly stated his desire to leave Atletico in favour of Barcelona, who had been working behind the scenes to sign him. However, despite Alvarez’s best efforts, Atleti blocked his dream move, refusing to let their talisman join a direct La Liga rival.

‌



They were, however, reluctantly open to selling him abroad as an alternative after it became very clear the forward had no desire to stay at the Metropolitano Stadium for another season. Reports indicated that Arsenal were heavy favourites to land Alvarez if he was willing to settle for a move to north London, after failing to secure one to Catalonia.

‌



But the 2022 World Cup winner did not want to move back to England, having played for City between 2022 and 2024. He will remain at Atletico, at least until January, despite months of wrangling with the club.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

8 controversial Mike Dean moments from row with Arsenal manager to celebrating goal READ MORE :

Man Utd, Arsenal and Liverpool name Champions League squads as Reds snub two senior stars READ MORE :

Yet, it has now been claimed that City sought to hijack their Premier League rivals Arsenal in the final days of the summer window by reaching out to Alvarez’s team in an effort to bring him back to the Etihad.

‌



The Athletic reports that a mini-saga played out ahead of deadline day, when several sources familiar with Alvarez’s situation indicated that City monitored developments last week to see whether a return was possible. City are claimed to have made an ambitious enquiry while they were pursuing Cody Gakpo and Iliman Ndiaye, who they eventually signed.

However, they did not receive any encouragement and pulled back. City themselves deny that they made an approach to the striker’s camp.

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez did not want to return to City despite his huge success there (Image: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

‌



Meanwhile, Radio Marca went further by saying the Premier League transfer record-equalling sum City spent on Enzo Fernandez on deadline day was first used for Alvarez. The Spanish outlet claimed a €150m (£129m) offer was made to Atletico - the figure widely reported to be their asking price.

That indicates a serious pursuit of the Argentine by City while many assumed Arsenal were the only team in the race for his signature. However, Alvarez is said to have turned down the offer by not even responding.

It is believed that his decision was as a result of either lifestyle preferences or documentation issues, which would have made it difficult for his family members to follow him to England. Alvarez famously won the Treble in his second season in Manchester.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
