The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has opened up an investigation into whether Tesla’s new self-driving Cybercab meets federal safety standards. The company launched the service in Austin, Texas on Thursday.

World.title: Witkoff and Kushner will travel to ‘end’ Russia’s war in Ukraine: Trump
World.content:
Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Russia and Ukraine this weekend to help restart peace negotiations.

Share Witkoff and Kushner will travel to ‘end’ Russia’s war in Ukraine: Trump on social media

United States President Donald Trump said that US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are travelling this weekend in an attempt to revive peace talks between Ukraine and Russia.

On Friday, while speaking at the White House, Trump said Witkoff and his son-in-law Kushner, who are preparing to travel to Kyiv and Moscow this weekend, are bringing a proposal to “end the war”.

“I sent Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner … to see whether or not we can get something done,” Trump said. “And there may be a good chance that we’ll do it.”

“We have an idea for peace,” Trump added without mentioning any specifics about his administration’s plan.

According to Russian state news agency TASS, Witkoff and Kushner will be in Moscow on Saturday and Sunday, their first visit since January.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also said the duo would be in Ukraine on Sunday, marking their first visit to the country since Trump returned to power.

Russian President Vladimir Putin recently said negotiations were “frozen”. But this weekend’s expected talks come as both sides continue to ramp up air attacks, with Russia hitting the headquarters of Ukraine’s SBU security services on Friday.

At least 12 people were injured in the strike, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said.

Al Jazeera’s Audrey MacAlpine, reporting from Kyiv, said that while people weren’t shocked the SBU building was hit, it has made them wonder what target might be next.

“It’s not so much that people never expected the SBU to be hit, but it really raises the question of if Russia can hit this, what else can it hit?” she said. “Some people here are wondering whether this attack, for example, could be aimed at possibly dissuading” the US envoys’ trips to Ukraine.



Trump told reporters Friday that a peace deal in the more than four-year conflict has remained elusive due to what he described as a “personality problem” between both sides.

“President Zelenskyy and President Putin truly hate each other,” Trump said. “They have serious hate, and it’s getting in the way.”

While exact figures are unknown, a study released in July by the Center for Strategic and International Studies says the war has cost Russia some 450,000 lives. Ukraine is estimated to have endured between 125,000 and 150,000 fatalities.

World.title: Sabalenka interrupts US Open match against Rakhimova over cannabis smell
World.content:
World number one Aryna Sabalenka had an unusual interruption during ⁠her US Open third-round ⁠match, stopping play to alert the umpire to a strong smell of cannabis drifting onto the Louis Armstrong Stadium court.

Sabalenka, who ⁠had made a fast start to go 3-0 ahead before securing a straight-sets win against Uzbekistan’s Kamilla Rakhimova, raised the issue during her second service game on Friday, pointing ⁠out the smell before play resumed.

“Someone is smoking weed,” top seed Sabalenka told umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore as she was serving 30-0 up. “Would you mind to… because it’s so strong.”

Sabalenka later told reporters she was not objecting to anyone enjoying themselves, but asked for the smoking ‌to be kept away from the court.

“I was like, Guys, you can do whatever, you can smoke whatever, you can relax as much as you can, but please to not do it around the tennis courts,” a smiling Sabalenka said. “It’s a bit tricky to handle that smell while you’re trying to compete at your best.”

The odour of cannabis has become a familiar — if unwelcome — feature at ⁠Flushing Meadows, with players complaining about the distraction in the ⁠past.

While smoking is not permitted inside the grounds, recreational cannabis is legal for adults 21 and older in New York, and smoke from people in the surrounding Flushing Meadows-Corona Park can drift into the tennis ⁠complex and onto the courts.

Sabalenka said she had smelled cannabis before during the tournament but never so strongly during a ⁠match, with Friday’s wind apparently carrying the odour into ⁠the stadium.



“That strong, yeah. Also, because it was a bit windy,” she said. “I don’t know if it was coming from the crowd or was from the outside because the wind blows it into the stadium.

“I ‌just hope they are a bit more aware of that stuff,” she added, before laughing when the questions returned to the subject. “Come on, guys. I think there is ‌nothing ‌else to say about weed. I’m just asking people not to smoke it next to the tennis court.”

World.title: Liverpool beat Ipswich as Isak goals hand Iraola first Premier League win
World.content:
Bradley Barcola makes his debut as Alexander Isak scores both Liverpool goals in 2-0 win at Ipswich Town.

Alexander Isak scored twice for Liverpool in their 2-0 Premier League win at Ipswich Town, handing Reds manager Andoni Iraola his first win since taking over in the summer.

Sweden international Isak pounced in the sixth and ninth minutes of Friday’s match at Portman Road to ease Liverpool nerves that a third successive winless match may be in the offing.

With his side in cruise control in the second period, Iraola was able to look to the bench to hand a 64th-minute debut to Bradley Barcola, who became the club’s record signing with his summer move from Paris Saint-Germain.

“We needed this win,” Iraola told Sky Sports. “It was also nice to get a clean sheet and control the match.

“The second half was not as good as the first, but we didn’t concede any chances.”

Isak’s first came courtesy of a drilled finish from within the area, having been picked out by Cody Gakpo, that even the glove of Kjell Scherpen in the Ipswich goal could not stop.

The Reds, who drew their first two games of the season, sliced through the home side’s defence with an outside-of-the-foot through-ball from Gakpo that set Isak on his way to dribble past Jacob Greaves before slotting home.

“We were talking about starting the game well. It was perfect for us to get those two quick goals,” Isak told Sky Sports.

“We are starting to get to the way we want to play. We want to be offensive. We could have scored more.”

Iraola replaced Arne Slot, who was sacked after one season in charge as the Reds’ title defence fell apart in the last campaign. The former Bournemouth manager saw his side stumble in their opening games at Newcastle United and at home to Nottingham Forest.



Ipswich, therefore, represented a serious trip hazard as a promoted side that won their first league game and took the lead in a bright start to their defeat at Old Trafford last week.

It was a dominant display from the Reds throughout, though, with a deserved clean sheet kept at the other end.

“We were more direct, which we wanted, in the start and we scored two great goals,” Liverpool captain and central defender Virgil van Dijk told Sky Sports.

Isak had a goal that would have marked his hat-trick ruled out in the first half, while Dominik Szoboszlai thought he had won a penalty to increase the lead in the second period – following a challenge from Leif Davis – but the Liverpool midfielder was ruled offside by VAR.

World.title: Nigel Farage heckled as he denies Reform UK took illegal funding
World.content:
Nigel Farage heckled as he denies Reform UK took illegal funding

NewsFeed Nigel Farage heckled as he denies Reform UK took illegal funding

Reform UK leader Nigel Farage was heckled by protesters on Friday, as he addressed the party’s conference in Birmingham. Farage dismissed the findings of an investigative report that appeared to show his party had accepted illegal foreign donations.

World.title: Europe targeted by spiralling campaign of sabotage - and Russia is the chief suspect
World.content:
As summer temperatures in Europe smashed records and many politicians shifted to holiday mode, Russia remained focused on its war.

Not only did its military attacks across Ukraine intensify last month, becoming ever more deadly for civilians, Russia also appears to have escalated its sabotage campaign across Europe.

This time, military and defence sector sites were the prime target.

A full month after drones packed with explosives were found at Leipzig's airport, used by Ukraine to transport military goods, Germany's interior minister has declared that "Russia is responsible".

Russia's President Vladimir Putin is demanding proof, as always, and his officials call the accusation "absurd".

But the drones were just a dramatic start. August then brought a series of suspicious fires at defence facilities from Italy to Estonia.

Some of the affected countries have already blamed Russia; others are still investigating and some fires may eventually be ruled accidental, exactly as such attacks are designed to seem.

Poland's interior minister is clear.

"There are many, many signals that Russia is changing its strategy and intensifying its activities, including terrorist and sabotage activities," Marcin KierwiÅski said, warning people to be on their guard.

World.title: 'A rare moment of joy': Nepal tunnel rescues bring hope for more flood survivors
World.content:
Two people have been rescued from a tunnel in Nepal more than a week after flash flooding hit the Nepal-Tibet border, killing more than 1,300 people.

Nepal's army is continuing its search for survivors, but mud and rocks are making rescue efforts difficult.

The BBC's South Asia correspondent Azadeh Moshiri, reporting from Nepal, describes how the rescues have given renewed hope to some families still waiting to find out what happened to missing relatives.

World.title: UK support for Falkland Islands 'unwavering' after Argentina restates claims, No 10 says
World.content:
It is not yet clear how or to what extent the sanctions will be imposed or tightened. In Argentina, a current law already allows for restrictions of activities of oil companies participating in projects considered unauthorised on the islands.

Two oil companies â Britain's Rockhopper Exploration and Israel's Navitas Petroleum â are due to begin extracting oil in the Sea Lion oilfield off the Falklands coast within two years, something Milei said Argentina could not allow.

A joint statement from the two firms on Friday said it had the valid licences granted by the government of the Falkland Islands, "and with the full support of the UK government."

The project is due to deliver its first oil in 2028, Rockhopper and Navitas said the partnerships' timetable would not be affected.

The Sea Lion oilfield, around 130 miles from the islands, contains an estimated 1.7 billion barrels of oil - described by Rockhopper as a field containing "highly marketable crude".

Milei also announced plans for a naval base in Tierra del Fuego in the south of Argentina, saying Trump and the US were "assessing their historical position in regard to the Falklands", which Argentina refers to as Las Malvinas.

"That is not empty words as they understand that Argentina is a reliable partner and a valuable ally for decades to come," he said, describing the UK as a nation "in decline".

On Thursday, President Trump hinted the US would not help the UK in any future Falklands conflict because Britain "had not been there to help me" during his war with Iran.

Trump's latest remarks on the islands come after he previously said the US position on the Falklands is one of many under review.

On Friday, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the UK would "resolutely uphold" the self-determination of the islands.

Writing on X on Friday, Miliband said the Islands would remain British as that is the "overwhelming position of the islanders."

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting also said Britain's commitment to the Falkland Islands was "absolute and unshakeable".

"Milei's statement overnight tells us more about domestic politics in Argentina than it does about the Falkland Islands," he wrote in his own post on X.

In an earlier statement, Downing Street said it was "not the first time" the Argentine government had made economic threats against the Falkland Islands.

"We are clear that the Falkland Islanders' right of self-determination extends to the right to exploit their own natural resources," it said.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said "Britain does not surrender to bullies".

"If (Milei) wants a stronger Argentina, he should build its economy, not threaten others."

Although the US is formally neutral, Washington provided support for Britain's campaign to retake the islands after the Argentinian invasion in 1982.

Argentine forces landed on the Falklands to stake a territorial claim in 1982, sparking a 74-day war over the territory as a British military task force ejected them.

The conflict led to the deaths of 255 British military personnel, three islanders and 649 Argentine military personnel.

In a sign of the ongoing tensions between the two countries over the issue, Argentina players celebrated their victory over England in the World Cup by waving a banner in support of their country's territorial claim.

World.title: Russia hits Ukrainian security headquarters in drone attack, Zelensky says
World.content:
"All emergency services are on the scene. Everyone affected will receive the necessary assistance," Zelensky added in a message on Telegram.

"I instructed Poklad to deliver an appropriate, tangible response and, where possible, one that mirrors this strike, to the Russians once everything is ready. Our military will support this response."

Images of the office widely shared online showed black smoke pouring from two windows on the front of the building.

Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha said the attack was a "major escalation that demands resolute responses".

"Moscow launched this strike during a renewed push for peace - laying bare its true rejection of diplomacy," he added.

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said five people had been hurt in the SBU attack, but did not elaborate on whether they were inside the offices.

A nearby cafÃ© was damaged and one customer was taken to hospital after the strike.

Stanislav Zavertaylo, co-owner of the popular Zavertailo chain, told the BBC that this was his third cafÃ© to have been damaged since the start of the full-scale invasion.

"Now I'm in shock because there's a lot of damage. All the windows are broken, there's a lot of glass, garbage" he added.

The Russian defence ministry also said on Friday it had struck a cargo vessel in the Ukrainian port of Chornomorsk and a tanker near Odesa.

In recent weeks Russia has escalated its daytime strikes on Ukrainian targets.

In many instances it has employed jet-powered drones which are faster and harder to intercept. It is not yet known which type of munition was used in this latest attack.

World.title: Steve Irwin's family celebrates 'superhero' dad, 20 years after shock death
World.content:
She described the impact of her father's death on her mother Terri and her younger brother Robert, 22.

"My mum lost the love of her life; my brother and I lost the greatest dad," she wrote. "Grief never truly leaves us; we walk alongside it every day."

Bindi also shared details on how her daughter connects with the grandfather she never got to meet.

"I have a 5-year-old daughter who watches his documentaries every morning. She feels utterly loved by her 'grandpa crocodile' without ever having met him."

Since Steve's death, the Irwins have continued to run Australia Zoo in Queensland.

"My dad left a lasting impact so poignant that it will ripple out for generations to come," Bindi wrote, saying his life and legacy were "worth celebrating".

She thanked Steve for being the family's "guardian angel" and signed off her message saying she loved him "with my whole heart".

Steve's wife Terri also took to social media to mark the day, posting an interview where the khaki-clad wildlife advocate recounted Bindi's birth and its impact on him.

"The most incredible wildlife encounter of my life was the birth of my daughter, Bindi," Steve says in the interview, with his signature enthusiasm.

The first time he held his newborn child, the inspiration for her name hit him.

"I was flabbergasted and it was then that her name evolved. I've gone, 'Bindi!' after my favourite crocodile, Bindi," he said, with a wide grin.

Robert Irwin also posted a tribute to his father, with a photo of Steve holding him when he was a baby, alongside the caption, "Your legacy is forever".

Last November, Robert was crowned the winner of US dance competition Dancing with the Stars, a decade after his sister won the same title.

World.title: Trump's peace envoys to visit Moscow and Kyiv over weekend
World.content:
US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will visit Russia and Ukraine this weekend, as efforts to end the war appear to be gathering pace.

Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed he will meet with the envoys on Sunday, after they visit Moscow on Saturday to hold talks with meet Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Witkoff and Kushner have led US President Donald Trump's efforts to broker a peace deal, but a gulf remains between the two warring sides.

"They are bringing with them a proposal to end the war," Trump told reporters when asked about the visits.

Earlier on Friday, Zelensky said a Russian drone hit the office of Ukraine's security chief Oleksandr Poklad in Kyiv. Poklad appears to be unharmed.

In a post on social media, Zelensky said he had ordered Poklad, who head the SBU security service, to respond "adequately" to the attack.

Witkoff and Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, have visited Russia multiple times, but the purported talks will be the first in Ukraine.

Zelensky said he would guarantee the safety of Russian airspace during the envoys' visit and called for Russia to do the same for Ukraine.

Russia's state news agency Tass said Witkoff and Kushner were "expected to arrive in Moscow and then to Kyiv... on 5-6 September", quoting a source.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov later told reporters: "I wouldn't announce anything, but when these contacts take place, we will inform you."

Meanwhile, Putin told an international economic forum on Thursday that "there are chances" a peace deal could be reached.

"First of all, Moscow and Kyiv must agree between themselves," he said.

But he showed no sign of backing down from his maximalist demands, which included more territorial concessions from Ukraine.

Kyiv and its European allies have repeatedly rejected Putin's terms saying they are tantamount to capitulation.

Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and currently controls about 20% of its territory.

World.title: Argentine couple to return Nazi-looted painting to rightful owner
World.content:
A painting which was stolen by the Nazis and only recovered in Argentina last year must now be returned to the heir of its rightful owner, a court has ruled.

The late-baroque Portrait of a Lady was lost for 80 years until it was spotted in photographs of a house for sale near Buenos Aires.

The house belonged to Patricia Kadgien, the daughter of a Nazi fugitive who had fled there after the Second World War, and she has now agreed to return the painting in exchange for not being prosecuted for concealing it from the authorities.

Portrait of a Lady was among over 1,000 artworks looted from the collection of Jewish art dealer Jacques Goudstikker after the Nazi invasion of the Netherlands in 1940.

His daughter-in-law and sole heir Marei von Saher intends for the painting to be exhibited on a temporary loan at the Holocaust Museum of Buenos Aires to spread awareness of the issue, Argentine newspaper Clarin reports.

Von Saher has previously said her family "aims to bring back every single artwork robbed from Jacques' collection, and to restore his legacy".

This painting was first recognised in August 2025 by the Dutch Algemeen Dagblad (AD) newspaper on an estate agent's website of a property in the coastal town of Mar del Plata.

It was hanging above a green sofa in the living room of Patricia Kadgien, whose father Friedrich Kadgien had been a top adviser to Hermann Goring, Adolf Hitler's deputy. Goring plundered thousands of works across Europe.

World.title: UN votes to adopt new world map to reflect Africa's true size
World.content:
The Mercator map was designed in 1569 by the Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator to help European explorers navigate across the world.

The distortion of his map is a result of the fact that it is impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart.

Whenever a map of the world is drawn, compromises need to be made.

The Mercator map shows the curvature of the Earth by making countries near the equator seem smaller than they are, with countries nearer the poles appearing bigger.

In an effort to correct this, a team of cartographers in 2018 created an equal area map they called the Equal Earth projection.

In February, the AU's 54 member states adopted it, and said it "more accurately represents the sizes of all continents, particularly Africa".

Online campaign group #CorrectTheMap said: "You could fit the United States, China, India, Japan, Mexico and much of Europe into Africa and still have land to spare."

Ahead of Friday's vote, Togolese Foreign Minister Robert Dussey told the Reuters news agency: "A fair world begins with a fair map."

Earlier he had told a UN briefing: "A map is never neutral. It shapes perceptions, influences how the place of peoples and continents in the world is understood."

He had the backing of the French Foreign Minister Jean-NoÃ«l Barrot, who said his ministry was going to stop using the Mercator map, external.

"Changing the map obviously doesn't change the world. But correcting a representation that distorts it is already an act of truth," he said.

But Yaryna Ferencevych, a US representative at the UN, said the resolution mocked the work and purpose of the UN General Assembly, external.

"Instead of focusing on genuine problems of international peace, prosperity, or good relations, this body is debating map projects from the 16th Century, and their role in promoting reparations and 'cognitive justice'," she said.

In March, the US was also critical when a resolution was adopted declaring the transatlantic slave trade "the gravest crime against humanity".

World.title: Peter Obi, Duke, others join Amaechi at late mother’s vigil Mass
World.content:
Presidential candidates Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and Donald Duke of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP) were among prominent Nigerians who joined former Governor Rotimi Amaechi of Rivers State at a memorial vigil Mass for his late mother, Mary Orduah-Amaechi, in Port Harcourt on Friday.

The Mass was held at the Corpus Christi Cathedral of the Catholic Church in Port Harcourt ahead of the burial of Mrs Amaechi, who died at the age of 89.

Mr Amaechi, a former Minister of Transportation, is the African Democratic Congress (ADC) vice-presidential candidate for the 2027 election.

Other dignitaries spotted at the Mass, streamed live on Facebook, included former Minister of Labour and Employment, Chris Ngige, and the governorship candidate of NDC in Rivers State, Dumo Lulu-Briggs

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Titi Abubakar, wife of the ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, and others had earlier arrived in Port Harcourt for the burial.

Amaechi’s mother died at 89

Mrs Amaechi died peacefully on Thursday, 16 July, according to a statement issued by her son’s media office.

The family described her as a devout Christian who devoted her life to her family, community and God.

The late matriarch was also described as a community and Christian leader who was widely respected for her kindness, warmth and support for those around her.

Following her death, the family appreciated friends, supporters, and well-wishers for their condolences and prayers.

Mrs Amaechi will be buried on Saturday at Ubima, their ancestral home in Ikwerre Local Government Area of Rivers State.

The gathering at Friday’s vigil brought together political figures from various opposition platforms, including Mr Obi and Mr Duke, as well as associates of Mr Amaechi and the ADC presidential candidate.

Mr Amaechi served as the speaker of the Rivers State House of Assembly from 1999 to 2007 and subsequently governed the state for two terms between 2007 and 2015. He later served as the transportation minister from 2015 to 2023.

World.title: Assault: Doctors call off strike at teaching hospital after apology, management intervention
World.content:
Doctors at the University of Uyo Teaching Hospital (UUTH), Akwa Ibom State, have called off their strike over the alleged assault of a doctor at the facility.

The Chairperson of the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA) in Akwa Ibom State, Tiemah Akpabio, confirmed the development to PREMIUM TIMES on Friday night.

Ms Akpabio said the decision followed a meeting of the state executive council of the association on Friday, after the family of the woman accused of assaulting a doctor tendered an apology and the hospital management intervened in the dispute.

She said the strike would officially end at 8 a.m. on Saturday, 5 September.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The family has made an apology. The management has also said they will look into matters of assault. A committee will be set up to forward ways to protect the workers in the hospital.

“Based on that, they have called off the strike,” she told PREMIUM TIMES.

The NMA chairperson said an official statement on the decision would be issued shortly.

Apology tendered

In a letter dated 2 September and addressed to the President of the Association of Resident Doctors, UUTH, Susana Adie apologised for her conduct during a visit to the hospital’s diabetic unit on 1 September.

Ms Adie said she regretted her conduct and acknowledged assaulting a doctor, Edidiong Ubia, while attempting to obtain clarification about her medical prescription.

She also retracted the unpleasant words she spoke during the incident and apologised to the doctor, the resident doctors’ association and the hospital community.

“I sincerely regret my actions and any unpleasantness that may have arisen from the incident,” she said in the letter.

She appealed to the resident doctors to accept the apology and prevent the incident from creating “continued tension and resentment” between her and the medical profession.

The apology came after the Association of Resident Doctors declared an indefinite strike on Wednesday over the alleged assault.

Another strike over safety concerns

The industrial action was the latest disruption at UUTH concerning health worker safety.

PREMIUM TIMES reported on Thursday that the resident doctors had commenced the strike after an elderly woman allegedly assaulted a house officer at the hospital.

The NMA had demanded that the hospital management and security agencies identify and bring those responsible to justice within 48 hours, while also calling for stronger security measures at health facilities.

The latest incident occurred barely four months after another crisis at the same hospital triggered industrial action by doctors.

In May, PREMIUM TIMES reported that doctors in Akwa Ibom embarked on an indefinite strike following a controversial operation by Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) operatives at UUTH.

The operation, which centred on the arrest of a senior hospital official, caused panic at the facility and disrupted clinical services.

The EFCC later apologised to the affected doctor and members of the medical profession, leading the NMA to suspend its strike.

The recurrence of industrial action over alleged assaults and safety concerns has heightened questions about the protection of healthcare workers at the federal tertiary hospital.

The federal government subsequently ordered measures to strengthen the protection of health workers nationwide following the May incident.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that a committee set up by the government found the UUTH incident was not isolated, identifying 18 cases of assault, intimidation or harassment across federal tertiary health institutions in the preceding 12 months.

With Friday’s decision, normal medical services at UUTH are expected to resume from 8 a.m. on Saturday.

World.title: 2027: PDP responds to Nwifuru, says Ebonyi doesn’t belong to one party
World.content:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ebonyi State has said the state does not belong to any particular political party and urged residents to defend democratic pluralism.

The party said they should also defend their constitutional right to choose their political leaders in 2027.

Chukwuma Igwe, state chairman of the PDP, said this in a statement issued on Friday in Abakaliki.

Gov Nwifuru’s ‘inciting’ remarks

The PDP chairman was reacting to Governor Francis Nwifuru’s remarks at the inauguration of newly elected local government chairpersons and their deputies, where he threatened to remove the local official if the APC loses the 2027 elections in their council areas.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“As a local government chairman, if you like, go and sleep so that another person will take over your house.

“You will not stop us (APC) from winning. But when we win, we will remove you,” the governor told the newly inaugurated chairmen.

The PDP chairman described the statement as a threat to democratic participation and political opposition in the state.

“This is not a political banter; it is an open charge to visit official hostility upon citizens for no offence beyond their choice of party.

“We regard this incitement for what it is: an invitation to bloodshed and avoidable hostility,” he said.

Mr Chukwuma urged security agencies to discharge their responsibilities impartially and protect citizens irrespective of their political affiliations.

He said the PDP would not be intimidated into silence, adding that the party would use lawful and constitutional means to defend its members, structures and democratic rights.

“The Ebonyi State PDP will not fret, and we will not be intimidated into silence.

“We reaffirm our resolve to resist, through every lawful and constitutional avenue open to us, any further assault upon our members or structures,” he said.

The chairman called on democratic institutions, civil society organisations and other stakeholders to pay attention to the political situation in Ebonyi ahead of the 2027 general elections.

“Let it be known that Ebonyi State does not belong to one political party; its security architecture does not exist to serve one political entity; that principle is non-negotiable,” Mr Chukwuma said.

He further said that the people should make the ultimate decision on the state’s leadership in 2027 through a free, fair, and credible electoral process.

You’re our enemy if you aren’t in the APC – Local council chairman

Apparently inspired by Governor Nwifuru’s controversial remarks, the newly sworn-in Chairman of Ohaukwu Local Government Area of Ebonyi State, Paul Ituma, a few days ago, warned opposition politicians to stay away from the council area ahead of the 2027 election or submit to his APC and the Ebonyi State governor

A video clip which showed Mr Ituma making the remarks surfaced on social media on Wednesday, barely 24 hours after Governor Nwifuru threatened to remove any chairman who fails to win his council area for the APC in the 2027 election.

Speaking at a meeting after his inauguration, Mr Ituma said that anyone opposed to Governor Nwifuru or the APC had become his enemy and should stay away from Ohaukwu LGA.

“Except maybe based on what the governor has said, the opposition wants to submit to us so that we can embrace them. Anybody who is not thinking in that direction should not come around Ohaukwu Local Government because Ohaukwu is cordoned off, and anybody who dares to do that will be declared persona non grata,” the chairman said.

Continuing, he said: “Anybody who wants to bring sand to put in my garri should not come to Ohaukwu. Anybody who is fighting the governor of Ebonyi State is my enemy from today and will be treated like an enemy.”

(NAN)

World.title: Court strikes out suit filed against APC candidate for Imo federal constituency
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja has struck out a suit filed by a member of the House of Representatives, Miriam Onuoha (Imo-APC), challenging the recognition of Uchenna Agasu as the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for the 2027 election.

Justice Salim Ibrahim, in a judgement, held that the court lacked the jurisdiction to hear and determine the case on the ground that a court of coordinate jurisdiction had determined a similar suit.

Justice Ibrahim, who upheld the preliminary objection filed by Mr Agasu, described the suit as “an abuse of court process.”

Although the judgement was delivered on 24 August, its certified true copy was made available to the News Agency of Nigeria on Friday.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Background

Ms Onuoha, who is the chairperson of the House of Representatives’ Committee on Tertiary Education Trust Fund, had filed the suit to challenge INEC’s recognition of Mr Agasu as the APC candidate.

She had named APC, Mr Agasu, and INEC as the 1st to 3rd defendants in the suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1568/2026.

The lawmaker, in the originating motion dated 20 July and filed by George Ibrahim, SAN, sought an order setting aside the purported upload of Mr Agasu’s name by INEC on its portal on 11 July as APC’s candidate for Isiala/Mbano/Okigwe/Onuimo Federal Constituency seat of Imo in the 2027 general elections.

Ms Onuoha sought an order directing the commission to forthwith upload her name as the APC candidate for the constituency seat.

She also sought an order of injunction restraining Mr Agasu from parading himself as the candidate of the party for the constituency seat, among others.

But APC and Mr Agasu disagreed with Onuoha’s submissions.

Mr Agasu, in his preliminary objection filed by his counsel, Paul Ananaba, SAN, prayed the court to dismiss the suit as a gross abuse of court process.

He argued that the court lacked the jurisdiction to hear the case on the ground that an Owerri court had, on 25 June, delivered a judgement on a similar case.

He further submitted that the earlier judgement remained subsisting and that the present proceedings amounted, in effect, to an invitation to the instant court to rehear a question already determined by another judge of the same court.

INEC’s position in the suit

INEC, in its affidavit of facts and written address filed by Johnson Usman, SAN, stated that it would abide by the court’s determination.

Mr Usman further explained that under the prevailing nomination arrangement, political parties themselves uploaded candidates’ particulars through the access granted by the commission.

He stated that the APC uploaded Mr. Agasu’s name on 11 July, and that name remained on the portal as of the hearing date.

Delivering the judgement, Justice Ibrahim said that before going into the substantive suit, the court would look at the preliminary objection filed by Mr Agasu in line with the previous Supreme Court decision.

He agreed with Mr Agasu’s submission that the Owerri suit and the instant case were on the same subject matter.

“This court does not express any opinion upon whether the judgement of Owoibo, J. was rightly or wrongly decided.

“An allegedly erroneous judgement is not thereby rendered nonexistent.

“Until set aside by a court invested with appellate authority, it remains a subsisting judicial determination which a court of coordinate jurisdiction is bound to respect.

“It follows that, having found that this court lacks jurisdiction to hear and determine the plaintiff/respondent’s substantive suit, the proper order to make in the circumstances is to strike out the instant suit.

“I therefore hold that, having regard to the subsisting judgement of the Federal High Court, Owerri Judicial Division, delivered by Hon. Justice I.N. Owoibo on 25th June, 2026, in Suit No. FHC/OW/CS/70/2026.

“The fact that the Federal High Court, by virtue of Section 19(1) of the FHC Act, which makes the court one, but based on administrative convenience, the Chief Judge divided the court into different divisions pursuant to the powers of the Chief Judge.

“See Orji v Chima (Supra) per KEKERE-EKUN, JSC (as he then was, now CJN) and also to the fact that this is a gross abuse of court process as this court is a court of coordinate jurisdiction with the Owerri division.

“I therefore find merit in the preliminary objection and hold that it ought to be sustained.

“Accordingly, I hereby sustain the preliminary objection and strike out Suit No FHC/ABJ/CS/1569/2026…There shall be no order as to costs,” the judge ruled.

(NAN)

World.title: Environmentalist calls for probe into Okrika deaths, action on gas leaks
World.content:
Environmentalist and climate justice advocate Nnimmo Bassey has called for an independent investigation into the deaths of at least 37 people reportedly involved in an illegal oil siphoning operation in Okrika, Rivers State.

The police in Rivers State confirmed the deaths but said they will continue to investigate the details.

“The Rivers State Police Command can confirm the deaths. The victims were allegedly attempting to steal crude oil,” the Command spokesperson, Blessing Agbabe, told DW News, a German international broadcast station.

Mr Bassey, in a commentary titled “Gassing the Niger Delta,” said the incident should prompt urgent action to address longstanding environmental and safety concerns in the oil-producing region.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The deaths were reported on Thursday at Okari Jetty in Okrika Mainland, where people suspected of illegal oil bunkering had gathered to load petroleum products. Community sources and the Youths and Environmental Advocacy Centre (YEAC-Nigeria) said at least 37 people died after inhaling fumes. Several others were reported missing.

Mr Bassey said the exact cause of the deaths remained unclear because, as of the time of his commentary, there had been no official or independent investigation into the incident.

“Obviously, the last breath of the dead may have been of noxious gases released under high pressure,” he wrote, adding that the victims might also have drowned after losing consciousness.

The YEAC-Nigeria Executive Director, Fyneface Dumnamene, called on the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA) to conduct an immediate Joint Investigation Visit to the site. He also urged the company whose pipeline was vandalised to improve security around its facilities.

Related incidents

Mr Bassey linked the Okrika deaths to the ongoing methane gas seepage in Bille, a fishing community in the Degema Local Government Area of Rivers State.

PREMIUM TIMES reported in June that gas has been bubbling from abandoned oil and gas infrastructure in Bille for nearly a year, threatening residents’ health and livelihoods. The report said preliminary assessments by NOSDRA indicated the presence of methane, volatile organic compounds and hydrogen sulphide in the ambient air.

Amnesty International, in a March report, said the gas has been bubbling since October 2025 in rivers, swamps and drinking wells in Bille. The organisation said the Nigerian government conducted an investigation but had not released the findings or taken action to stop the leaks.

In May, Amnesty said residents were still facing a serious health emergency and that the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission had begun an investigation. It called for the findings to be made public and for the leaks to be stopped.

Mr Bassey, in his commentary, said, “As we write this, the gas is still dangerously emitting in the community and could erupt in flames at any time. There have been some palliatives or relief materials by the government, and the provision of a fire truck that cannot access much of the community.

“We also hear of the provision of fire extinguishers in the community. These are all laughable actions in the face of an impending tragedy. Visitors to Bille end up getting sick within a short period of time. Residents, especially children and the elderly, develop illnesses at rates that signal something toxic is happening in the community and that the risks extend beyond possible fire outbreaks.

“Truth is that the Bille community is being gassed while the government and the oil companies are wringing their hands and watching from the sidelines. I recall hearing a minister of state on television claim that there were no oil facilities in Bille. Such crass, obnoxious ignorance!”

He also cited the fire at the Ororo-1 oil well, offshore Awoye in Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, which began in May 2020.

A PREMIUM TIMES report in April noted that the fire was still burning more than six years after the incident. NOSDRA earlier said the fire followed an explosion during workover operations on the well.

Mr Bassey said the Okrika deaths should not become another tragedy that attracts attention only until the victims are buried.

“The dead will be buried. They will be branded criminals, and perhaps rightly so. But we all know that oil thievery is an industrial activity with a long value chain, and players, so to speak,” he wrote.

Mr Bassey called for the cleanup of the Niger Delta, the removal of decrepit oil facilities and the replacement and burial of pipelines.

He also demanded the implementation of the Bayelsa State Oil and Environment Commission report and called for a just transition away from dependence on crude oil.

“Our lives are worth more than crude oil,” he said.

PREMIUM TIMES has reported on the environmental and regulatory concerns in the region. In a September 1 investigation, this newspaper found that weak enforcement of anti-gas-flaring laws had allowed oil companies to continue flaring gas, with oil-producing communities bearing the environmental and health costs.

World.title: Enugu youths unite against terror, declare support for war on insecurity
World.content:
Residents and youths of Enugu State on Friday marched through popular streets in the state capital in support of the government’s campaign against insecurity, declaring their zero tolerance for terror, criminality and violent extremism.

The youths, including undergraduates and members of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), who ultimately converged at Government House, Enugu, where they were received by the Enugu State Governor, Dr. Peter Mbah, pledged to mobilise young people across the state against criminal activities and violent extremism.

Addressing the group, Mbah said security was one of the recurring risk factors identified by his administration while mapping out the developmental building blocks for the state, hence his decision to tackle the menace head-on from the outset.

While commending the youths for taking the initiative to support the anti-crime efforts of the President Bola Tinubu Administration and the Enugu State Government, the governor said his administration’s “Tomorrow Is Here” mantra was not a mere political slogan, but a commitment to investing in young people who would take charge of the state’s future.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“For you to march through the streets and end here preaching the message against crime and terrorism is profound. Ordinarily, we should be the ones preaching to you against such vices.

“But by this act, you are telling us that you are not going to be on the fringes or stand by and watch. Rather, you are going to be at the forefront of the campaign against cultism, crime and terrorism,” the governor said.

Mbah said greater involvement of youths in the fight against criminality would lead to a significant reduction in crime, freeing up resources for job creation and poverty eradication.

He noted that some countries had shut down many of their correctional facilities after recording significant reductions in crime, stressing that a similar transformation could be achieved in Nigeria when young people took ownership of the campaign against criminality.

The governor said the state had adopted a zero-tolerance policy towards criminality, adding that a safer Enugu would attract more investors and generate other multiplier effects for the economy.

He urged the youths to take their campaign against crime and terrorism to every part of the state, saying their initiative would send a strong message that criminality was no longer fashionable among young people.

According to him, the government would complement the youths’ campaign through non-kinetic interventions, including job creation, increased investment in education and digital skills development.

“Your campaign is heartwarming. When citizens apply scholarly and constructive approaches, government will be glad to engage them constructively and productively too,” Mbah said.

Earlier, a leader of the march and Deputy Rector of the Institute of Management and Technology (IMT), Enugu, Dr Emeka Ejim, described the coalition as a broad-based youth movement comprising corps members and students united by a common agenda to campaign against crime, cultism and terrorism.

Ejim pledged the group’s support for the state government’s security efforts, saying Enugu had distinguished itself in the fight against crime and cultism through a combination of kinetic and non-kinetic measures, including skills acquisition and job creation.

“We pledge never to join bad groups within and outside Nigeria. We are joining you against terrorism,” he said.

Also speaking, the Enugu State leader of the National Association of Nigerian Students (NANS), Okeke Kelvin, said the association would mobilise no fewer than two million youths to support the campaign against violence and terror.

“This is the only way we can show you that we are against terror. We say no to terrorism,” Kelvin said.

The student leader commended the state government for investing heavily in modern security infrastructure in the state, noting the settingup of the Command and Control Centre, Centre for DNA Forensics and Criminal Investigation, Distress Response Squad DRS), and others, which he said were yielding results.

“For instance, they tried you at Affa in Udi, and in no time the kidnappers realized they cannot ply their trade in Enugu State,” he stated.

NYSC corps members Olaranju Oreose and Emmanuela Momoh expressed gratitude to Governor Mbah for the peace and security they enjoy in Enugu, saying the state had totally changed their views and allayed the fears they initially nursed when posted to the South East region.

“I am Olaranju, representing the General CDS President. Sir, as a corps member from the South West, and I have been in Enugu from January till now, I want to say that my journey and experience so far here has been wonderful in terms of security.

“Initially, I had the fear of coming this far distance to Enugu. But having been here, I have changed that thinking. I want to let you know that no one amongst us here, no matter the tribe, no matter the religion, is supporting terrorism.”

World.title: EFCC arraigns two over alleged £110,000, N500 million fraud in Lagos
World.content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has arraigned Ali Bala and Yusuf Umar Anka before the Lagos State High Court in Ikeja over alleged fraud involving £110,000 and N500 million.

The defendants were brought before trial judge Olukayode Ogunjobi on 10ncounte of money laundering, stealing and retention of stolen property. EFCC spokesperson Dele Oyewale stated this in a statement on Friday.

One of the counts alleged that the defendants, sometime in 2025 in Lagos, conducted financial transactions involving proceeds of unlawful activity in an attempt to conceal the source of £110,000 allegedly stolen.

One of the counts alleged that Mr Bala, a.k.a. Barrister Ahmed, and Mr Anka sometime in 2025 in Lagos, “conducted financial transactions involving proceeds of your unlawful activities to disguise the source of the stolen £110,000.00…”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The EFCC noted that the alleged offence contravened Section 7(1)(b)(i) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act, 2006.

Messrs Bala and Anka pleaded not guilty to the charges.

After their pleas, prosecution lawyer, H.U. Kofarnaisa, asked the court to adjourn the case for trial and sought an order for the defendants to be remanded in a correctional facility.

But the defence lawyer told the court that applications for the defendants’ bail had already been filed.

Mr Ogunjobi fixed 8 September for hearing of the bail applications. He ordered that the defendants remain in EFCC custody until then.

The antigraft agency has recently prosecuted the defendants who have been involved in fraud.

In February, Daniel Osiagor of the Federal High Court in Lagos convicted two Chinese: Huang Haoyu and An Hongxu, to 46 years’ imprisonment each for cyber terrorism and internet fraud.

During their trial, EFCC noted that the defendants were found to have procured and employed Nigerian youths to falsely represent themselves as foreign nationals for the purpose of defrauding unsuspecting victims through online platforms.

Also, EFCC prosecuted three individuals and two companies over an alleged theft of N652.18 million. The commission secured the conviction of four persons for illegal foreign exchange transactions and unlawful trading of naira notes.

It also recovered N125 million for a victim of an alleged land fraud in Lagos.

World.title: Police arrest 699 suspects, recover 31 firearms in Ebonyi
World.content:
The police in Ebonyi State, Nigeria’s south-east, say they have arrested 699 suspects in connection with 372 cases from April 2026 to date.

The state’s Commissioner of Police, Hope Okafor, revealed this on Thursday in Abakaliki during a press conference on the command’s operational achievements.

Mrs Okafor said the arrests comprised 660 males and 39 females.

Of these figures, 309 suspects have been charged in court in connection with 162 cases, while investigations into the remaining cases are ongoing.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“The command recovered 31 assorted firearms, 33 rounds of ammunition of different calibres and three vehicles,” she said.

The police commissioner remarked that the command had stepped up surveillance and intelligence efforts around known flashpoints throughout the state.

“We have deployed personnel strategically to such locations to forestall breaches of peace and ensure the safety of residents.

“These strategies have helped to reduce the number of skirmishes encountered in the state drastically,” she said.

She warned against criminal activities, emphasising that there would be no refuge for those involved in kidnapping, murder, and other violent crimes in Ebonyi.

On this note, the command will persist in deploying intelligence-led policing and ongoing operations to identify, arrest, and prosecute criminal elements within the state,” Mrs Okafor said.
